(Dallas, Texas) * [[Link Academy (Missouri)|Link Academy]]
([[Branson, Missouri]]) | college = [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]] (2022–2023) | draft_year = 2023 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 38 | draft_team = [[Sacramento Kings]] | career_start = 2023 | years1 = {{nbay|2023|start}}–present | team1 = [[Boston Celtics]] | years2 = 2023–2025 | team2 = → [[Maine Celtics]] | highlights = * [[List of NBA champions|NBA champion]] ([[2024 NBA Finals|2024]]) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2022 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2022]]) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2022) }} '''Jordan Walsh''' (born March 3, 2004) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Boston Celtics]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). A [[guard (basketball)|guard]]–[[forward (basketball)|forward]], he played one season of [[college basketball]] for the [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas Razorbacks]] after being a consensus five-star recruit and a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]]. The [[Sacramento Kings]] selected him with the 38th overall pick in the [[2023 NBA draft]] and traded his draft rights to Boston. Walsh was a member of the Celtics' [[2024 NBA Finals|2024 NBA championship]] team. ==Early life and high school career== Walsh was born and raised in [[DeSoto, Texas]].{{cite web |title=Jordan Walsh Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and more |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/w/walshjo01.html |website=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=July 11, 2026}} He attended Faith Family Academy in Dallas for his first three years of high school.{{cite web |title=NBA 2023 Draft Prospects: Jordan Walsh |url=https://www.nba.com/draft/2023/prospects/jordan-walsh |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 11, 2026}} As a freshman, he made the game-winning dunk in the 2019 Class 4A state championship game to give Faith Family its first state title.{{cite news |last=Gosset |first=Brian |date=March 14, 2019 |title=Faith Family freshman, who won state on buzzer-beating dunk, not letting Alopecia stop him |url=https://www.star-telegram.com/sports/dfwvarsity/article227461714.html |work=[[Fort Worth Star-Telegram]] |access-date=February 10, 2023}} As a junior, Walsh averaged 18 points, 11 rebounds, five assists, 2.4 steals and 2.3 blocks per game and was named Class 4A All-State by the Texas Association of Basketball Coaches.{{cite news |last=Munz |first=Jason |date=September 24, 2021 |title=Memphis basketball recruiting: 5-star Jordan Walsh taking official visit |url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/college/memphis-tigers/basketball/2021/09/24/memphis-basketball-recruiting-5-star-jordan-walsh-official-visit-penny-hardaway-larry-brown/5834067001/ |work=[[The Commercial Appeal]] |access-date=January 22, 2023}} Walsh transferred to [[Link Academy (Missouri)|Link Academy]] in [[Branson, Missouri]], before his senior year.{{cite news |last=Riddle |first=Greg |date=September 6, 2021 |title=Four-star basketball recruit Jordan Walsh leaves Faith Family, now at prep academy in Missouri |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/high-school-sports/basketball/2021/09/06/four-star-basketball-recruit-jordan-walsh-leaves-faith-family-now-at-prep-academy-in-missouri/ |work=[[The Dallas Morning News]] |access-date=January 22, 2023}} He averaged 15.3 points, 7.2 rebounds and 3.1 assists per game and was named the 2022 MaxPreps Missouri Player of the Year.{{cite web |title=Jordan Walsh |url=https://arkansasrazorbacks.com/roster/jordan-walsh/ |website=Arkansas Razorbacks |publisher=University of Arkansas Athletics |access-date=July 11, 2026}}{{cite web |last=Divens |first=Jordan |date=March 24, 2022 |title=High school basketball: MaxPreps Player of the Year in all 50 states |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/p0UAhQj8q0iWR3GgkizMKg/high-school-basketball-maxpreps-player-of-the-year-in-all-50-states.htm |website=[[MaxPreps.com]] |access-date=February 5, 2023}} Link Academy finished as the runner-up at the 2022 GEICO Nationals. Walsh was selected for the [[2022 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] and the 2022 [[Jordan Brand Classic]].{{cite web |last=Orange |first=Alyssa |date=January 25, 2022 |title=Nick Smith Jr & Jordan Walsh named McDonald's All-Americans |url=https://www.fox16.com/sports/local-sports/nick-smith-jr-jordan-walsh-named-mcdonalds-all-americans/ |website=[[KLRT-TV|FOX16.com]] |access-date=January 22, 2023 |archive-date=January 22, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230122222341/https://www.fox16.com/sports/local-sports/nick-smith-jr-jordan-walsh-named-mcdonalds-all-americans/ |url-status=dead}} ===Recruiting=== Walsh was a consensus five-star recruit and a consensus top-25 player in the 2022 class.{{cite web |last=Boone |first=Kyle |date=October 14, 2021 |title=Arkansas basketball recruiting: Five-star SF Jordan Walsh commits to Razorbacks |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/arkansas-basketball-recruiting-five-star-sf-jordan-walsh-commits-to-razorbacks/ |work=[[CBS Sports]] |access-date=February 10, 2023}} ESPN analyst [[Paul Biancardi]] rated him as the best two-way player in the class.{{cite news |last=Davenport |first=Richard |date=May 23, 2022 |title=ESPN's Biancardi names Hog signee top 2-way player |url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2022/may/23/espns-paul-biancardi-names-hog-signee-top-two-way-player/ |work=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]] |access-date=January 22, 2023}} Walsh committed to Arkansas over offers from [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]], [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]], [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]] and [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]].{{cite web |last1=Borzello |first1=Jeff |last2=Biancardi |first2=Paul |author-link2=Paul Biancardi |name-list-style=and |date=October 14, 2021 |title=Jordan Walsh, ranked No. 7 in the 2022 class, announces commitment to Arkansas |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/32401700 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |access-date=January 22, 2023}} {{College Athlete overall = 11 | accessdate = July 11, 2026 | bball = yes }} ==College career== [[File:Jordan Walsh (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|upright|Walsh in 2023]] Walsh began his freshman season at Arkansas in the starting lineup but moved to a reserve role during conference play.{{cite news |last=Murphy |first=Tom |date=January 22, 2023 |title=Hogs find their 'D' vs. Rebels |url=https://www.arkansasonline.com/news/2023/jan/22/hogs-find-their-d-vs-rebels/ |work=[[Arkansas Democrat-Gazette]] |access-date=January 30, 2023}} He appeared in all 36 games, made 22 starts and averaged 7.1 points, 3.9 rebounds and 1.1 steals per game as Arkansas reached the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] Sweet 16. On April 19, 2023, Walsh declared for the [[2023 NBA draft]] while maintaining his college eligibility.{{cite web |last=Wayne |first=E. |date=April 19, 2023 |title=Arkansas forward Jordan Walsh declares for NBA Draft |url=https://razorbackswire.usatoday.com/2023/04/19/arkansas-forward-jordan-walsh-declares-for-nba-draft/ |work=[[USA Today]] |access-date=June 30, 2023}} He announced on May 31 that he would remain in the draft and forgo his remaining college eligibility.{{cite web |last=Goodson |first=Connor |date=May 31, 2023 |title=Jordan Walsh not returning to Arkansas, remaining in 2023 NBA Draft |url=https://razorbackswire.usatoday.com/2023/05/31/arkansas-basketball-jordan-walsh-not-returning-to-razorbacks-remains-in-2023-nba-draft/ |work=[[USA Today]] |access-date=June 30, 2023}} ==Professional career== The [[Sacramento Kings]] selected Walsh with the 38th overall pick in the second round of the [[2023 NBA draft]]. The Celtics acquired his draft rights and the [[Dallas Mavericks]]' 2024 second-round pick in exchange for the draft rights to [[Colby Jones]], who had been selected 34th overall.{{cite web |date=June 28, 2023 |title=Boston Celtics Complete Trades |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/boston-celtics-complete-trades |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 11, 2026}} Boston announced Walsh's signing on July 6, 2023.{{cite web |date=July 6, 2023 |title=Boston Celtics Sign Walsh |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/boston-celtics-sign-walsh |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 11, 2026}} The contract was reported as a four-year, $7.6 million deal with a team option for the fourth season.{{cite web |last=Simone |first=Jack |date=July 6, 2023 |title=Celtics sign rookie Jordan Walsh to four-year, $7.6 million contract |url=https://www.celticsblog.com/2023/7/6/23786335/boston-celtics-sign-rookie-jordan-walsh-four-year-7-6-million-contract-second-round-exception |website=CelticsBlog |access-date=July 11, 2026}} Walsh made his NBA debut on January 17, 2024, recording four rebounds in the final three minutes of a 117–98 win over the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite news |last=Terada |first=Souichi |date=January 18, 2024 |title=Celtics rookie describes unforgettable NBA debut |url=https://www.masslive.com/celtics/2024/01/celtics-rookie-describes-unforgettable-nba-debut.html |website=MassLive.com |access-date=December 9, 2024}} He scored his first NBA points on February 4 in a 131–91 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite news |last=Himmelsbach |first=Adam |date=February 5, 2024 |title=Celtics rout depleted Grizzlies in what originally had the potential to be a battle of top teams |url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2024/02/04/sports/grizzlies-celtics-td-garden/ |work=[[The Boston Globe]] |access-date=February 5, 2024}} During his rookie season, Walsh also played 27 regular-season games, all starts, for the [[Maine Celtics]] of the [[NBA G League]], averaging 14.7 points and 7.5 rebounds per game. He appeared in five G League playoff games as Maine reached the [[NBA G League Finals]].{{cite web |title=Jordan Walsh |url=https://www.nba.com/player/1641775/jordan-walsh/bio |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 11, 2026}} Walsh was a member of Boston's 2024 NBA championship team, appearing in three games during the Celtics' playoff run. He played three more games for Maine in 2024–25, including two postseason games.{{cite web |last=Martin |first=Spencer |date=December 5, 2025 |title=Jordan Walsh's perfect night leads Boston in blowout win |url=https://maine.gleague.nba.com/news/jordan-walshs-perfect-night-12042025 |website=Maine Celtics |access-date=July 11, 2026}} Walsh's role increased during the 2025–26 season, when he appeared in 68 games and made 25 starts while averaging 5.4 points and 4.0 rebounds per game. On December 4, 2025, he scored a career-high 22 points on 8-of-8 shooting, along with seven rebounds, three assists, two steals and one block, in a 146–101 win over the [[2025–26 Washington Wizards season|Washington Wizards]]. On June 29, 2026, Boston exercised its non-guaranteed $2.4 million team option on Walsh's contract for the 2026–27 season.{{cite web |last=Dalzell |first=Noa |date=June 29, 2026 |title=Celtics make roster decisions on Neemias Queta, Jordan Walsh |url=https://www.celticsblog.com/boston-celtics-news/142561/celtics-roster-neemias-queta-jordan-walsh |website=CelticsBlog |access-date=July 11, 2026}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend|champion=y}} ===NBA=== Sources:{{cite web |title=Jordan Walsh Traditional Stats |url=https://www.nba.com/stats/player/1641775/traditional |website=NBA.com |access-date=July 11, 2026}} ====Regular season==== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;
